DNA (blue) nuclei: 10-15% of interphase cells have markedly enlarged nuclei and many cells show bi/multinucleation, lobed contours and clusters of small micronuclei puncta vs uniformly oval single nuclei in DMSO. reflection.text:
Unblinding: vincristine, CHEMBL90555 Tubulin inhibitor (target CHEMBL2095182) per e17/e18 - 'Microtubule destabilizers' class. Verdict incorrect: I submitted Aurora kinase inhibitors 0.62 then 0.58 over Microtubule destabilizers 0.28/0.34.

What got it right:
The quantitative atlas comparison was right and I under-weighted it. e5: 1/2 NSC Microtubule destabilizers; e8 after 4 wells: 3/4 NSC Microtubule destabilizers. The critique notes similarities 0.903-0.985 for those votes - that should have outweighed qualitative labels. The raw morphologies were also consistent with the truth: e2 10 uM tub_std z=+21.4, e7 act_std z=+16.2, e3/e6/e7 nuc_solidity z -33.4 to -46.6, nuc_form_factor z -23.8 to -39.5, frac_large_nucleus z +14.3 to +21.6. I discounted tub_std as generic disorganization, but in retrospect high-dose tubulin variance increase is expected for a tubulin inhibitor/destabilizer. e11/e9/e10 dose_response were non-significant (rho +0.20 p=0.8 for solidity, rho -0.80 p=0.2 for large nucleus, rho +0.40 p=0.6 for mitotic_like over n=4 wells) and should not have been used to discriminate.

What misled me and why:
1. Microscopist descriptions e4 and e14: both gave 'candidates: Aurora kinase inhibitors' based on lower density and 8-9 observations described as grape-like micronuclei/polyploidy. I treated those NLP candidate labels as ground truth in e12/e15 hypotheses (0.62, 0.58), despite the known phenotypic overlap between Aurora failure and microtubule destabilizer-induced cytokinesis failure/mitotic slippage that both produce large, irregular, multilobed/micronucleated nuclei and solidity loss. My e20 literature search for that exact overlap returned 0 hits, so I made the distinction without support, rather than recognizing the overlap as non-discriminative.

2. Over-interpretation of negative evidence: I used e11 frac_mitotic_like rho +0.40 p=0.6 as 'without mitotic arrest favoring Aurora' and e10 negative trend as polyploidy signature. With only 4 acquired wells spanning 0.03, 0.3, 1, 10 uM and p>0.2, the trend was noise. Microtubule destabilizers can show transient arrest then slippage to polyploidy, so lack of monotonic increase does not exclude them. I also ignored that k-neighbour Protein synthesis 5-6/10 votes in e5/e8 indicated noisy nearest neighbours at high toxicity (e2 only 130 cells at 10 uM) but NSC vote was still stable for Microtubule destabilizers.

3. Acquisition choice: I front-loaded budget on single replicates at 4 doses (highest dose first to see max phenotype e2, then mid/low) and requested no additional orthogonal image channel or concentration replicates. I then re-acquired a second describe_phenotype e14 on the already-acquired 0.03 uM well w_3415990e66 per review request, which simply confirmed the first microscopist bias rather than providing independent tubulin polymer or phospho-H3Ser10 readouts. I acknowledged the atlas strongly favored runner-up in rationale e16 but still submitted Aurora.

Lesson: When NSC similarities are >0.9 for 3/4 wells, that quantitative signal should dominate a single qualitative phenotype label, especially for vincristine where literature confirms microtubule destabilizer mechanism - e.g. microtubule depolymerization phenotypes PMID 35436470 and microtubule dynamics disruption PMID 27760837 and mitotic arrest sensitivity PMID 36967563. The proposed follow-up of p-H3Ser10/p-Aurora plus tubulin polymer quantitative imaging would have directly discriminated Aurora B substrate loss from tubulin inhibitor polymer loss, rather than relying on shared nuclear morphology.

I also ignored that k-neighbour Protein synthesis 5-6/10 votes in e5/e8 indicated noisy nearest neighbours at high toxicity (e2 only 130 cells at 10 uM) but NSC vote was still stable for Microtubule destabilizers.

3. Acquisition choice: I front-loaded budget on single replicates at 4 doses (highest dose first to see max phenotype e2, then mid/low) and requested no additional orthogonal image channel or concentration replicates. I then re-acquired a second describe_phenotype e14 on the already-acquired 0.03 uM well w_3415990e66 per review request, which simply confirmed the first microscopist bias rather than providing independent tubulin polymer or phospho-H3Ser10 readouts. I acknowledged the atlas strongly favored runner-up in rationale e16 but still submitted Aurora.

Lesson: When NSC similarities are >0.9 for 3/4 wells, that quantitative signal should dominate a single qualitative phenotype label, especially for vincristine where literature confirms microtubule destabilizer mechanism - e.g. microtubule depolymerization phenotypes PMID 35436470 and microtubule dynamics disruption PMID 27760837 and mitotic arrest sensitivity PMID 36967563. The proposed follow-up of p-H3Ser10/p-Aurora plus tubulin polymer quantitative imaging would have directly discriminated Aurora B substrate loss from tubulin inhibitor polymer loss, rather than relying on shared nuclear morphology.
